# Swarmail

> An SMTP mail mock built for a program waiting on mail, not a human at a web UI:
> a single Rust binary that accepts any SMTP
> traffic on :1025 and exposes captured email through REST, MCP and a web UI on
> :8025. Every accepted message is queryable immediately — there is no async gap
> where mail can be lost.

## Getting started

- SMTP: point any client (Ory Kratos, Nodemailer, curl) at `localhost:1025`. No
  auth required; if the client authenticates, the **username names the inbox**
  (per-test isolation). A server started with `--route-domain <domain>`
  (SWARMAIL_ROUTE_DOMAIN; decision 0112) routes by recipient instead:
  `<local>@<label>.<domain>` is stored in inbox `<label>`, outranking the AUTH
  username, so parallel agents behind one sending identity stay apart. Mint a
  private address with the `swarmail_create_inbox` tool. A recipient under the
  domain that names no inbox is refused 550 5.1.3; a second routed inbox in one
  transaction is 452 4.5.3 (retry it as its own message).
- POP3: plain RFC 1939 on `localhost:1110`. `USER <inbox>` names an existing
  swarmail inbox — the maildrop is the inbox, so mail delivered over SMTP is
  readable over POP3. STAT/LIST/UIDL/RETR/DELE/RSET/TOP/CAPA/QUIT; DELE takes
  effect on QUIT. Plaintext only.
- MailHog / Mailpit clients: point them at `http://localhost:8025` — the
  well-known read endpoints are answered from the same store (see the shims
  section below).
- HTTP: API at `http://localhost:8025`, this file at `/llms.txt`, OpenAPI at
  `/openapi.json`, MCP at `POST /mcp`, health at `/healthz`, Prometheus at `/metrics`.
- Binds: all three listeners default to `127.0.0.1` (the image and the chart
  state `0.0.0.0` explicitly). While the HTTP listener is loopback-bound, two
  headers are checked before the router: a `Host` that is not a loopback
  spelling of the bound port is refused 403 — the DNS-rebinding defense, since
  a rebound page sends same-origin requests with no `Origin` while its Host
  still spells the attacker's name — and a present `Origin` that is not a
  loopback spelling of the bound port is refused 403 (a browser cannot forge
  it). No `Origin` (curl, agents, the stdio bridge, every harness) passes the
  Origin leg untouched; every client names its Host honestly. A `Host` with
  no port means 80; a portless loopback `Origin` still refuses.
- Off loopback (`0.0.0.0`, the image and the chart): the Host allowlist is
  inactive, but a present `Origin` must name the request's own `Host`
  authority (same host, same port; an omitted port means the Origin scheme's
  default, 80 or 443), else 403 `cross-origin requests must match the Host
  authority`. Requests with no `Origin` pass. A reverse proxy must forward the
  original `Host`, port included; `X-Forwarded-*` is ignored. This is not
  authentication: any network peer is trusted and DNS rebinding is not
  prevented. A forwarded port (`ssh -L`, VS Code, Codespaces) refuses on a
  loopback bind; the remedy is an off-loopback bind such as
  `SWARMAIL_HTTP_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8025`, which the operator owns.
- `/metrics`: `swarmail_http_requests_in_flight` counts the scrape itself
  (quiet server reads 1). Label values use only the `\\`, `\"`, `\n` escapes.
- Pages are capped at 250 items on every plane: `limit`/`count` above it is
  refused with a 400 (REST + shims) or a `-32602` error (MCP), never clamped.
  `GET /api/v1/inboxes` (and the UI index) pages with `limit` (default 100)
  and `offset`; MCP `swarmail_search_emails` pages with `offset`.
  SMTP request parsing and every compat list/search build (scan, render,
  serialization) run off the async workers on the blocking pool; the MCP
  seed build, the REST list/await pages and SSE thread-view serialization
  stay inline (none is on the ingest path).
- Strict native input: existing closed list/count/await/assert/thread/feed
  query shapes accept only their documented keys. Ten further methods take
  no query keys: `DELETE /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/messages`,
  `DELETE /api/v1/delete-all`, `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}`,
  `DELETE /api/v1/messages/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/raw`,
  `GET /api/v1/chaos`, `DELETE /api/v1/chaos`, `GET /api/v1/webhooks`,
  `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks`, and `POST /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/seed`. Each
  unknown, bare or empty-valued key is a native JSON 400 naming method,
  route and decoded key; no query and a literal empty query preserve behavior.
  A bad seed query follows syntax/media/size/data-shape body errors but
  precedes domain validation of a deserializable body. Unsupported destructive
  selectors never scope clears; body-based selective deletion uses the ids body.
  Compat list/search tolerance, selective DELETE, chaos/webhook PUT and
  health/metrics/UI/document routes keep their own contracts. An unknown key
  in a seed or webhook body (`subjet`, `secrt`) is refused by name with HTTP
  400. An unknown MCP tool argument key (`{"inbx": "zz"}`) returns JSON-RPC
  `-32602` in HTTP 200 for a call with an `id`; valid notifications remain
  silent. A present JSON `null` for an optional string (seed `from`/`subject`/`text`/
  `html`, webhook `inbox`/`secret`/`ca_pem`, chaos `error`) is refused,
  omission takes the default. Seed and webhook JSON data errors are `400`
  with a JSON `error`. Malformed JSON syntax stays the extractor's plain-text
  `400`, missing/wrong media type its plain-text `415`, and oversize its
  plain-text `413`. Chaos JSON data errors stay the extractor's `422`.
  A blank inbox name, or one with a control character, is refused on every
  plane (SMTP AUTH and POP3 USER included), and any other name is kept verbatim, padding included.
- The Mailpit/MailHog compat list and search routes keep their upstream
  tolerance: unknown query keys are ignored, so a typo such as
  `/api/v1/messages?inbx=` answers the whole store. The compat `latest`
  routes refuse unknown keys.
- The `to` filter matches any recipient: the To/Cc headers **and** the SMTP
  envelope (RCPT TO), so a Bcc'd address matches — `assert?to=x&count=0` is
  not a header-presence check. `from` is the header From. Every email also
  carries `envelope_from` (the MAIL FROM path; `""` for `<>`, `null` for mail
  stored before it was kept).

## The agent loop (clear → act → assert)

1. `DELETE /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/messages` — start clean.
2. Trigger the flow (signup, reset, invite...).
3. `GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/await?to=user@x.io&count=1&timeout_ms=5000` —
   blocks until the mail arrives (push-based; no sleep-polling). Returns the email.
   `count` means "at least one" — even `count=0` waits rather than succeeding
   instantly (decision 0010). `timeout_ms` above 60000 is refused with 400,
   never clamped, and a stopping server answers the wait with 503
   `shutting down` instead of parking (decision 0018) and refuses new
   mutations with their usual 503 `storage commit failed`, nothing
   applied (decision 0024).
4. Assert subject/body: fields `subject`, `text`, `html` are on every email; the
   `links` array holds every URL and `codes` holds likely OTP/verification codes —
   no regexing HTML required. `codes` keeps at most the first 64 distinct codes
   (mail stored before the cap keeps its array verbatim); text and HTML that
   are direct `multipart/alternative` siblings yield the text's codes (the
   HTML's only when the text has none), other bodies contribute in source
   order. A quoted attribute's link ends at its own closing quote, so an
   encoded `&#39;` or `&quot;` inside `href` stays in the URL. Exact counts: `GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/assert?count=N`
   answers 200 only when exactly N mails match — `assert?count=0` is the negative
   assertion ("nothing arrived"), 200 on an empty filter and 409 with
   expected/matched otherwise; counts are never clamped to one.
5. `POST /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/seed` injects a synthetic email (full parse +
   extraction pipeline) — fixtures without SMTP. A given `html` body is preserved
   verbatim and supersedes `text`; envelope fields containing CR, LF or NUL are
   refused before anything is stored.

## MCP


Revisions: 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25. Single initialize returns a
supported proposal, newest-supported 2025-11-25 for an unsupported string,
or legacy 2025-03-26 for omission; supplied non-strings refuse -32602.
Clients send Content-Type: application/json and Accept: application/json,
text/event-stream, then MCP-Protocol-Version: <returned revision> after init.
HTTP is stateless: missing version header means 2025-03-26; one supported
header selects its revision. Invalid/duplicate/unsupported headers refuse
400/-32600/null after POST body/parse checks, also on other methods except
OPTIONS: a guard-admitted OPTIONS is 405 with Allow: POST and no CORS (decision
0043 §4). Media-header leniency is retained.
No sessions or SSE; GET /mcp is 405 with valid or absent version headers.

Only 2025-03-26 supports batches; every batch description below refers to
that revision. Modern arrays refuse one -32600/null before all effects,
including notification-only arrays. Legacy batch initialize stays legacy.
Modern tools annotate the twelve reads (search, get, latest, wait, both extracts,
the deliverability report, whose cache fill changes no mail, both focused
waits, the inbox minter, which allocates nothing, and both attachment tools)
readOnlyHint:true and the six mutations readOnlyHint:false,
destructiveHint:true (delete, both clears, seed, which can prune, and both chaos
changes, which replace configuration).
For 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 every tool declares an object-root outputSchema.
Every success returns structuredContent plus the same JSON in its existing text
block; text-only consumers can keep reading content. Errors keep their text/RPC
shapes without structured success data. March (also missing-version requests)
keeps its thirteen existing catalogue entries and existing result bytes;
discovery appends the two focused waits and swarmail_create_inbox after them,
sixteen in all, then the two attachment tools, eighteen in all. Tests pin the
REST-backed schemas to served OpenAPI through explicit output projections,
including omitted fields and nullable provenance; the focused waits and the
attachment tools are MCP-only
and their schemas are checked against independently stated expectations.
Compact reads (decision 0108): on 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25,
swarmail_search_emails and swarmail_get_latest_email answer a compact view per
email by default: id (the handle for swarmail_get_email), from, to, subject,
received_ms, a snippet of at most 200 characters, codes, anchors (url,
anchor_text) and attachments (filename, content_type, size), no bodies. Lists
of anchors and attachments are cut at 250 with the exact anchors_total or
attachments_total. A "attachments": null means unknown: mail stored before attachments were
captured, or a body the parser could not read. Mail stored before link
occurrences were kept serves its stored links instead of anchors. get_email and wait_for_email stay whole. The four reads (search,
latest, get, wait) take fields: an array of names from the published enum; each
email then carries the named members it has plus id, in the server's fixed key
order; [] is ids only; text and html appear only when named; an unknown name or
a wrong type is -32602 before any lookup or wait. March has no fields. REST:
GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/messages?view=compact answers the same
{total, emails} envelope with compact items; compact is the only value, and
without it the list is unchanged. Token impact is not measured here (no paid
trial).
Dual output costs bytes/tokens: the bridge retains its 10 MiB response cap and
returns -32000 when exceeded, even when the March text alone would fit. Use smaller
pages; one large Email can still exceed the cap. Lost mutation replies do not
mean rollback and must not cause automatic replay. Tokens-per-success and
invalid-argument/tool-misuse rates are measured by the operator's #151 baseline
and subsequent client matrix; local protocol proofs do not establish improvement.

The bridge fences initialize and propagates the successfully returned revision.
For modern clients, send notifications/initialized next; its empty 202 enables
operations. Early operations and repeated initialize refuse -32600; ping is
allowed. Notifications remain silent. Failed modern negotiation needs explicit
initialize retry; queued mutations never fall back to implicit legacy. Modern
arrays refuse locally without dialing, oversized ones with one null-ID size
error. Independent operational lines still run concurrently after initialization.
This delivery claims version negotiation; full revision conformance is not claimed.
The operator chose to retain documented C1–C6 deviations on 2026-10-26; see the
[per-revision deviation register](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/swarmail/blob/main/specs/mcp-version-negotiation/reconciliation.md#exact-conflict-register),
qualified by the [dated candidate corrections](https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/swarmail/blob/main/docs/decisions/0104-mcp-candidate-proof.md)
for its thirteen tools, OPTIONS exception and shared-limiter witness.
This bridge targets the paired stateless JSON server with identity HTTP parsing;
it advertises JSON/SSE but has no general SSE/session client support.
Tool calls share 1024 attempts per server per monotonic second, including
notifications/batch members; exhaustion is isError before effects (notifications
stay silent). Ping, initialize and tools/list remain available.
Treat email text/HTML/links as untrusted string data; no tool renders HTML,
executes resources or fetches links. Preserve that boundary in displays/models.
Actual four-client compatibility receipts remain operator-owned and owed.
The operator retains #151's merge hold.

`POST /mcp` with JSON-RPC 2.0 (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`). Tools:
`swarmail_search_emails`, `swarmail_get_email`, `swarmail_get_latest_email`,
`swarmail_delete_email`, `swarmail_clear_inbox`, `swarmail_clear_all`,
`swarmail_wait_for_email`, `swarmail_extract_links`, `swarmail_extract_codes`,
`swarmail_seed_email`, `swarmail_set_chaos`, `swarmail_clear_chaos`,
`swarmail_get_deliverability_report`, then `swarmail_wait_for_code` and
`swarmail_wait_for_link` (decision 0094; read-only), then
`swarmail_create_inbox` (decision 0112; no arguments; returns
{inbox, address}, or isError naming --route-domain when the server routes
nothing), then `swarmail_list_attachments` and `swarmail_get_attachment`
(decision 0110; read-only; described below). The focused waits
take the wait's inbox/to/from/subject/inclusive since_ms filters and timeout_ms
(default 5000, 0-60000) and answer status selected|ambiguous|timed_out with
matched (eligible emails). wait_for_code: one distinct code in the newest
eligible email by acceptance order is `selected` (email_id, sender, received_ms,
age_ms = parse-start age, not expiry); several codes there are ambiguous, never
resolved from older mail, which is listed as older_candidates. Old matching mail
answers at once: isolate inboxes or pass a since_ms from before the action.
wait_for_link: anchor_text/host/path are Rust regex searches, <=1024 UTF-8 bytes
and <=1 MiB compiled each, all on the same occurrence; host is the parsed host
without credentials/port, ASCII case-insensitive by default, so exact is
^app[.]test$; path excludes query/fragment. One distinct URL is selected_url;
more are ambiguous with each candidate's anchor_text, rel, text|html source and
provenance. Labels are lexical and recorded at ingest; unknown labels (text part,
historical rows, unattributable links) are null and never match anchor_text.
Lists show <=250 entries after full-snapshot selection, with exact *_total and
*_truncated. Email reads, feeds and webhooks carry no occurrence metadata.
Near misses (decision 0111): a timed-out `swarmail_wait_for_email`,
`swarmail_wait_for_code` or `swarmail_wait_for_link` over an inbox that holds mail
also carries near_misses, read from the store at the timeout, no extra retention:
arrivals (retained mail the wait did not answer with, newest first, <=10, exact
arrivals_total and arrivals_truncated), nearest_subject (an entry or null) and
last_arrival_ms (received_ms of the newest retained mail, ignoring since_ms). An
entry is email_id, received_ms, from, to (<=5 distinct To/Cc/envelope addresses,
exact to_total), subject and missed, the supplied to/from/subject filters that
mail fails (a sibling address reads ["to"], a typo ["subject"]); strings are
clipped to 256 bytes. wait_for_email lists only mail its filter refused; the
focused waits list every retained mail, missed [] meaning it passed your filters
but had no code or no selected link. since_ms limits arrivals. nearest_subject is
a hint, never a selection: the mail that missed the subject alone with the most
shared character pairs; read its to. No near_misses key means the inbox holds
nothing. Own inbox only; not access control (MCP is unauthenticated).
Attachments (decision 0110): swarmail_list_attachments {id} answers
{id,total,truncated,attachments}, <=250 entries in message order and <=3 MiB of JSON,
so labels that escape heavily can list fewer (total is exact; a stored part cut from
the answer stays fetchable by index),
each {index,filename,content_type,size,sha256,stored,ics}: type lowercased, size
in decoded bytes, sha256 lowercase hex of exactly the bytes get returns. Candidates
are the parser's attachments plus any text/calendar, application/ics or .ics part;
an attached message is one entry. ics is the FIRST VEVENT's dtstart, dtstart_tzid,
dtend, dtend_tzid, summary (unescaped) and uid, verbatim, no timezone resolution;
null for no VEVENT, non-UTF-8 or >1 MiB. swarmail_get_attachment {id,index} answers
{index,filename,content_type,size,sha256,encoding,content}: encoding utf-8 for valid
UTF-8 without control bytes beyond tab/LF/CR, else base64; never truncated. Only
1 MiB of decoded bytes is kept per mail, first-fit in list order; a larger part is
listed with stored:false and fetch refuses it, naming its size, the budget and
GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/raw, which serves the whole mail. Strings are cut to 1024
bytes. Mail stored before the feature answers unknown, even where a compact read
shows its attachment labels; nothing is backfilled.
stdio transport: `swarmail mcp --url http://127.0.0.1:8025` (launch as an MCP
subprocess; talks to the same server). Except for malformed seed fixture
content and the supplied `timeout_ms`
refusal described below, wrong-typed or malformed MCP arguments and unknown
argument keys return JSON-RPC `-32602` in HTTP 200 for a call with an `id`,
before any effect. An elapsed `swarmail_wait_for_email` timeout is a normal
tool result: `isError: false`, with `matched`, `total` and `timed_out: true`
in its text content. On `swarmail_wait_for_email`, a supplied `timeout_ms`
must be an integer from 0 through 60000; malformed values and values above
60000 return an HTTP-200 tool result with `isError: true` and refusal text,
not a JSON-RPC `error` object.
`swarmail_seed_email` refuses `CR/LF/NUL` in its `to`, `from` or
`subject` fixture strings before insertion under decision
[0010 §2](docs/decisions/0010-exact-count-asserts-and-the-shared-seed.md);
for a call with an `id`, it returns HTTP 200 with a tool result
`isError: true` whose text names the offending field and its reason;
no message is inserted. Wrong-typed seed arguments and unknown keys
remain JSON-RPC `-32602`; id-less notifications stay silent.

Tool failures such as `shutting down` return
`isError: true` with an error message in text content.
An unknown MCP argument key returns JSON-RPC `-32602` in HTTP 200 for a call
with an `id`, before any effect. Other protocol and
argument refusals use a JSON-RPC `error`: bad JSON
or invalid UTF-8 is HTTP 400 `-32700`, a body over 2 MiB is HTTP 413 `-32600`, a
non-object value — or an id-less object without a string `method` — is
`-32600` with a null id (once per batch member). The stdio bridge dials
port 80 for a portless URL and refuses a body over 2 MiB itself, `-32600`
with the request's own ids, without sending it. The up
to 16 members of a batch run concurrently — replies keep member order, the
effects have no order, so send dependent mutations as separate requests.

## Chaos

`PUT /api/v1/chaos` with e.g. `{"data": {"probability": 30, "error": "451 4.3.0
tempfail", "delay_ms": 250}}` — inject SMTP failures to test your retry logic.
`DELETE /api/v1/chaos` disables it. Wire values are never narrowed:
`probability` must be an integer 0..=100, a supplied `error` must be a
single-line 4xx/5xx SMTP reply of at most 510 octets (a `2xx` error is
refused — a rule that would answer success while the mail is not stored is
a lie), and `delay_ms` is 0..=300000; each refusal names its rule with the
same sentence on both the REST and MCP planes (decision 0025/0029).

## Webhooks

`PUT /api/v1/webhooks` with `[{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:9999/hooks", "secret":
"s3cret"}]` (omit `inbox` for every inbox) — every accepted email is POSTed as
`{"event":"received","email":{...}}` with the secret in `X-Swarmail-Secret`;
queued, retried 4x (100ms → 1.6s), never awaited by SMTP acceptance. Delivered via
reqwest + rustls: `http://` targets stay plain, `https://` targets are TLS
with certificate verification on — for a self-signed test server, pass its
CA in the target's optional `ca_pem` (PEM of a root to trust on top of the
built-in root store). A target is validated at PUT (a 400 naming the
defect: the keys are exactly `url`, `inbox`, `secret`, `ca_pem`; the URL
must parse with an http/https scheme and a host; every certificate in
`ca_pem` must load into the delivery client — at least one, a bundle's
later roots included — which proves loadability, not that a handshake will
succeed; the `secret` must be a single-line header value ≤4096 octets) and
a refused list leaves the previous one in place. `GET /api/v1/webhooks`
redacts the secret, strips URL userinfo and returns `ca_pem` as canonical
validated certificate blocks only (unrelated PEM sections and prose are
omitted; certificate DER, order and duplicates are retained). A supplied
bundle that cannot be fully projected is an empty string; absent values stay
`null`. Mixed PEM admission remains unchanged. The echo is diagnostic, not a
body to PUT back. Server CA work (#220) uses two process-wide dedicated native
workers, no pending queue, and a 64 MiB logical charged-job budget. GET, PUT and
custom-CA delivery misses share immediate admission without fairness. GET/PUT
503 is `webhook CA preparation unavailable`; valid oversized inputs can refuse,
including permanent GET refusal for oversized directly installed state until
replaced/cleared. Admitted failures retain GET 500 `webhook response preparation
failed`, PUT 500 `webhook configuration preparation failed`, and invalid PUT 400.
Failed/refused/cancelled PUT preserves installed state. Delivery refusal spends
one of four ordinary attempts. Jobs/results remain charged after cancellation
until disposed; worker threads live until process exit and stop does not drain
them. Finite work reclaims across Tokio runtime replacement. CA jobs cannot
consume SMTP/Store blocking slots; OS scheduling/latency/fairness are not promised.
The logical tariff is not an allocator/RSS ceiling: HTTP extraction, installed
state, existing dispatcher snapshots/payload, transferred responses/cache,
transport, stacks and synchronous embedder helpers are excluded. Builds remain
outside the cache mutex; builds_total counts actual successful delivery builds,
including losers/cancelled owners, never API builds/hits. Admission/build time
is outside the 22.1-second network/backoff sum. Delivery is bounded
per target — 32 in flight per normalized URL (`WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_CAP`), so
a stalled sink cannot consume another sink's delivery slots; the bound is per URL, so many
distinct targets multiply the ceiling (a target-count cap is not implied),
a refused fan-out is counted
in `swarmail_webhook_dropped_total` (its `warn` names the refused target),
a spent retry budget in
`swarmail_webhook_exhausted_total` (its final refusal logged as a `warn`
naming the target and the cause), and a shutdown's undelivered backlog in
`swarmail_webhook_aborted_total` — counted, never silently lost.

## Threads and the live feed

- `GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/threads` — the inbox grouped into conversations:
  References/In-Reply-To/Message-ID chains first, the normalized subject
  (leading Re/Fw/Fwd/Aw/SV/VS/Antw/WG/TR/RV/Odp/R/I/ENC/RES/Ответ/回复
  markers stripped with `:` or `：`, whitespace runs collapsed,
  Unicode-lowercased — full case folding and numbered `Re[2]:` are
  recorded limitations) as the fallback for chain-less mail; each thread lists its mails
  oldest first and has a stable `key` for
  `/api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/threads/{key}` — the hash of the conversation's
  first mail's anchor, so replies (even one with a smaller message-id) never
  move an advertised URL. Threads are recomputed per request: pre-existing
  mail is re-keyed once on the next request, no migration.
- `GET /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/feed` — server-sent events, one `threads` event
  per change carrying the full thread view as JSON (the first event is the
  snapshot; a lagging watcher is repaired with a recomputed view). The web UI
  is built on these: `/ui/inbox/{inbox}` and `/ui/inbox/{inbox}/thread/{key}`
  update live, no manual refresh.
- Thread fields (`message_id`, `in_reply_to`, `references`) are extracted at
  ingest and stored on every email, so views never re-parse raw headers.

## MailHog / Mailpit API shims

Same store, the two shapes existing suites already speak:

- `GET /api/v1/messages` — Mailpit's summary envelope (`total`, `unread`,
  `count`, `messages_count`, `messages_unread`, `start`, `tags`,
  `messages`), newest first by receive time then id — every compat list,
  search and `latest` share that order, scoped or not (the native inbox list
  keeps acceptance order, which can differ). `?inbox=` scopes to one swarmail inbox;
  `?limit=`/`?start=` page (`limit` ≤ 250, refused with a 400 above).
  Snippets read at most the first 8192 bytes of a body.
- `GET /api/v1/message/{id}` — Mailpit's full message; `/plain` serves the
  text part as text/plain, rendering html at request time for html-only
  mail. `GET /api/v1/message/latest` (and `/latest/raw`, `/latest/headers`)
  is the newest mail by receive time then id, scoped by `?inbox=` (404 when
  that inbox is empty) or the whole store without it; a nonblank `?query=`
  is a 400 — search, then fetch the id; Mailpit's `?tz=` is a 400 naming it.
  `DELETE /api/v1/messages` deletes exactly the
  non-empty `{"ids": [...]}` named mails (the `IDs` spelling accepted
  alike) and replies `{"removed": n}`; any
  other body (absent, empty, unparseable, `{"ids": []}`) is a `400` that
  deletes nothing — MailHog's bodyless wipe included (decision 0011);
  `DELETE /api/v1/delete-all`, swarmail's own route, is the HTTP
  plane's only cross-inbox wipe. The opt-in MailSlurper listener
  (`--mailslurper-listen`, off by default, its own port) has the other:
  `DELETE /mail` with `{"pruneCode":"all"}` clears every inbox (decision
  0118).
- `GET /api/v2/messages` — MailHog's `{total, count, start, items}` with
  `data.Message` shapes (`Content.{Headers,Body,Size,MIME}`,
  `Raw.{From,To,Data,Helo}`); a page whose JSON would pass 64 MiB is
  refused whole (`compat page exceeds byte budget 67108864; reduce limit or
  fetch raw by id`). `GET /api/v2/search` takes
  `kind=from|to|containing` (present and one of the three, as upstream
  requires) and answers a bare 400 on an unknown kind, an absent kind or
  an empty query; `?limit=`/`?start=` page. `GET /api/v1/search` is the
  Mailpit flavor
  (`kind=from|to|subject|containing`, JSON `400`). A containing query
  refuses field syntax by name — any word like `to:x` or `foo:x`, also
  behind Mailpit's `(`, `-`/`!` and `"` wrappers (`-to:x`, `"to:x"`,
  `(to:x)`), a URL's `://` excepted; there is no negation or quoting
  grammar.
- `GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/download` and `GET /api/v1/message/{id}/raw`
  serve the full RFC 5322 source as `message/rfc822`
  (`attachment; filename="<id>.eml"`).
- Mapping: Mailpit `Username` = the swarmail inbox; MailHog `From`/`Raw.From`/
  `kind=from`, Mailpit `ReturnPath` and `Return-Path` = the SMTP envelope
  sender (`""`/`<>` for a bounce; the header From only for mail stored
  before the envelope was kept); `Read` is always `false` and unread counts mirror `total`
  (no read state); tags are `[]`; attachments/inline are empty arrays. The
  swarmail-native `/api/v1/messages/{id}` is unchanged — the Mailpit-style
  single message is the singular `/api/v1/message/{id}`.

## Guarantees

- **Lossless bursts**: SMTP acceptance is synchronous — `DATA` ending with a 250
  means the message is stored and queryable. Verified in CI by
  `the_burst_guarantee` (1000 mails / 50 concurrent sessions, exact count).
- **No sleep-polling**: `await` is long-poll backed by per-inbox broadcast
  watchers; agents block until arrival instead of guessing delays.

## Deliverability report (decision 0085; epic #251)

GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/deliverability takes only the optional query key reachability (see Opt-in link reachability below) and returns
{rule_set_id, findings:[{rule_id,severity,location,fix_hint}], dns}. Severity is
info < warning < error. Locations are tagged header {name,occurrence:null|u64},
mime_part {path:[u64]} or link {part_path:[u64],byte_offset:u64}; link locators
are transfer-decoded source-byte coordinates, not URLs. Reports are sorted by
rule, typed location, severity and hint, with exact duplicates removed.
The bulk-sender checklist adds seven source-citing rules (first versioned swarmail-bulk/1, now part of swarmail-html/8):
one_click, message_id and date are errors; plain_text is warning-level presence
advice. DMARC policy presence, From alignment and passing aligned DKIM-or-SPF
are independent checks. They read six facts that the report evaluator computes
from the stored bytes, the SMTP envelope observed at ingest, DKIM's verdicts and
the declared DNS policy (SPF and DMARC, below). A fact that cannot be determined
is Unknown, and its entry is an error-level *.not_evaluated.v1 finding that
explicitly says "Not evaluated:". Sender-written Authentication-Results and
DKIM-Signature never supply evidence. A message qualifies at a threshold only when
every finding is below it, so a wait or an exact zero assertion matches mail whose
SPF, DKIM and DMARC evidence passes and whose checklist is clean at that
threshold; exact zero assertions count qualifying messages when every required
analysis succeeds; an analysis failure aborts the assertion. Waits still require a
qualifying message.

Headers use original bytes and complete singleton values, with root lowercase
names and occurrence null/0/1 for absent/invalid/duplicate. Message-ID and Date
support current RFC 5322 syntax and surrounding comments/folding; obsolete-only
forms are unsupported by this checklist, not universally invalid Internet mail.
Date validates calendar and weekday, numeric zones and optional seconds (including
60), without a clock/freshness check. Message-ID checks syntax, not uniqueness.
One-click requires a complete URI list containing HTTPS and the exact case-sensitive
List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click value. This structural check
proves neither signed-header DKIM coverage nor endpoint operation; no URI is fetched.
Text advice checks genuine outer sender text/plain, including empty/default/encoded
bodies and nested inline multiparts, excluding attachments/ancestry and embedded
message bodies (including multipart/digest defaults). It proves neither content
equivalence nor an unconditional provider mandate. HTML is never converted here.
Hints cite https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126 and
https://senders.yahooinc.com/best-practices/ plus applicable RFC 8058, 5322, 2046
or 7489 sections. These are fixed published references, not live verification or
provider certification. The rule record is decision 0089.

`swarmail-html/8` retains the synthetic demo.marker.v1: the first root
X-Swarmail-Demo field, unfolded and space/tab trimmed, selects info|warning|error
and emits "Remove the X-Swarmail-Demo header." The seven HTML rules are
html.css.position.v1, html.css.display-flex.v1, html.element.video.v1,
html.img.alt-missing.v1, html.image-only.v1, html.gmail-clipping.v1 and
html.tracking-pixel.v1. They warn on literal position CSS, display:flex/inline-flex,
video, absent alt (empty alt passes), image-only HTML and clipping risk; a remote
HTTP(S) img with explicit integer width/height each 0 or 1 gets an info disclosure.
Each affected HTML MIME part contributes at most one finding per rule, at its
structural child-index path (root []). Plain-text alternatives do not cure HTML.
Attachment/filename-bearing subtrees and attached messages are excluded.

Clipping means strictly more than 104448 decoded UTF-8 HTML bytes per part
(102 KiB), after transfer/charset decoding and before entity decoding; this is
an approximate Gmail risk heuristic, not its live boundary or an SMTP limit.
The applicability matrix covers Gmail web/mobile, classic Outlook for Windows
(Word renderer), and Apple Mail macOS/iOS. CSS rows target classic Outlook;
video targets Gmail and classic Outlook. There is no Apple-specific unsupported
feature row. New Outlook is different; unlisted features are unassessed.

The embedded, versioned catalogue src/deliverability/html-rules.json names
Can I email (CSS position/display:flex and HTML video), WHATWG alternative-text,
Mailchimp Outlook/Gmail-clipping guidance, and MDN Tracking pixel. Its summaries
are Swarmail-authored heuristics dated 2026-10-26, not an imported dataset or
fresh client-version measurements; current empirical measurements were not
supplied. Source URLs, client scopes, selectors, thresholds and fixed hints are
tracked there. No runtime network access or new dependency is needed.

Five per-link rules (decision 0121, issue #258) read each visible a href
of the eligible HTML parts: link.scheme.unsafe.v1 (error: javascript, vbscript,
data, file), link.url.invalid.v1 (warning: empty or not absolute; #fragment never
fires), link.scheme.http.v1 (warning: plain http except localhost and loopback),
link.shortener.v1 (warning: exact host in the built-in swarmail-shorteners/1 list)
and link.anchor-host-mismatch.v1 (warning: the label names a host the target is
neither equal to nor a subdomain of, after www. is stripped). A link finding is
located at link {part_path, byte_offset}, or at mime_part {path} when the part's
decoded text is not a prefix of its transfer-decoded bytes followed only by ASCII
whitespace. The default report fetches no link; empty
link findings do not mean the links are safe.

Opt-in link reachability (decision 0121). Off by default: start the server with
--link-reachability public|loopback (SWARMAIL_LINK_REACHABILITY), then ask with
GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/deliverability?reachability=true. On an off server that is
400 "link reachability is not enabled" and opens no connection; a missing message is
404. MCP, the message page, assert and await never probe, and SMTP never does. public
contacts only addresses a default-deny policy proves globally routable (IANA
special-purpose registries read 2026-11-04): IPv6 only inside 2000::/3 minus 2001::/23,
2001:db8::/32, 2002::/16 and 3fff::/20 (so fec0::/10, NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo are
refused), IPv4 only outside the non-global registry blocks; an address that embeds IPv4
is refused, never decoded. loopback also permits 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 (mail can then
cause GETs to local ports). URLs with credentials are never contacted. The check runs on
every redirect hop. Residual: a block IANA later allocates inside 2000::/3 is
contacted until the table is edited. Bounds: 5 s per target across all
hops, 2 s connect, at most 5 redirects, at most 32 distinct targets (more is 503
"deliverability analysis failed"), 4 targets at once per request, 2 probe requests per
Service, one per server process (a third is 503 "deliverability analysis unavailable"). GET only, headers
only, no body, no proxy, no cookies. Findings: link.redirect-chain.v1 (info; count and
final origin), link.reachability.v1 (warning; timeout, connect/DNS/TLS failure, HTTP
status 400 and above, redirect cap, or a missing/invalid/non-HTTP redirect) and
link.reachability.refused.v1 (info). The observation is composed into that response
and never cached, so two probes at different times may differ.

This finite lexical model respects source quotes, comments, CSS strings/functions
and nested media blocks. Hidden conditional comments and template content are
inert; head style blocks are checked. CSS escaped identifiers, cascade, layout,
CSS visibility and CSS-only pixel sizing are unassessed. Hidden text can defeat
image-only detection, and decorative tiny remote images can trigger disclosure.
A lone pixel can receive both image-only and tracking findings. Empty findings
do not certify client compatibility. Empty findings do not imply deliverability
or authentication success.
CSS declaration values retain balanced braces, parentheses and brackets as
opaque components; unused custom-property text cannot create declarations.
Literal unquoted url(...) keeps slash-star as URL data, with bounded escape/
whitespace validation. Malformed supported syntax still fails, including an
unclosed head or recognized tag and stray CSS closers; there is no browser repair.
Exactly zero stored raw bytes contribute no HTML findings before MIME parsing.
The historical demo/HTML composition returns {"rule_set_id":"swarmail-html/2",
"findings":[]} for that message; other collectors and report limits still run.
This historical result makes no authentication claim. In the current combined
report, SMTP accepts and stores an exactly empty message, but its missing MIME
metadata makes analysis fail: REST returns 503 and MCP returns isError.
Assertions and waits needing that report also fail rather than count it clean.
Nonempty parse failures still fail.
Analysis is lazy from stored bytes, off SMTP; extraction stays at ingest.
The existing message page renders the same report without polling.

DNS policy (decision 0120). Report checks that need DNS answers (DKIM keys, SPF,
DMARC; #254, #255, #256) read a declared, offline TXT map, never the network.
Every report carries a required `dns` member
{source:"default"|"server"|"inbox", policy:{txt:[{name,values}],tempfail:[name],spf_client_ip?},
lookups:[{name,type:"txt",outcome:"records"|"no_records"|"temp_fail",values}]}.
`policy` is the complete canonical effective policy; `lookups` lists each name an
evaluation resolved, once, sorted. DKIM verification (decision 0125, below) records
every key, ATPS and report name it asks for that lies inside decision 0120's name grammar (an out-of-grammar name fails closed and is not recorded); a message with no `DKIM-Signature`
records none, and SPF and DMARC (decision 0126, below) record the TXT names they ask for
(the record, its `include:` and `redirect=` targets, an `exp=` name, and the `_dmarc` names of the tree walk). `temp_fail` is never a pass and never clean: a report with a
`temp_fail` lookup qualifies at no no_findings_at_or_above threshold, so an assert
does not match it and a wait rides to its deadline. `no_records` is a definite
negative. The same message under the same configuration gives byte-identical
report JSON; no path, time or generation appears (the two stated exceptions are the
DKIM wall-clock residual, `dkim.expired_since_receipt.v1`, whose radius is
described below, and SPF's 20-second monotonic lookup timer, below).
Declare a server map with `serve --dns-policy FILE` (env SWARMAIL_DNS_POLICY): a
JSON file of at most 8192 bytes, `{"txt":[{"name":"s1._domainkey.example.com",
"values":["v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=..."]}],"tempfail":["_dmarc.example.org"]}`; `{}` is
an empty map and source "server". The declaration also takes an optional
`spf_client_ip`, an IPv4 or IPv6 address literal (stored canonical, present in
`dns.policy` only when declared) that SPF evaluates instead of the connecting
address the SMTP session saw; see SPF and DMARC below. A bad file stops startup before any listener
binds; there is no fallback to an empty map. Declare an inbox map with
PUT /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/dns (same body; 200 echoes the object
{"inbox","source","policy"}; 400 for an invalid declaration or an inbox label over
512 bytes, 413 for a body over 8192 bytes, 503 when 4096 inboxes already hold one)
and clear it with DELETE /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/dns (idempotent; it echoes the
fallback, the server map else the default). An inbox map replaces the server map;
there is no merge. A declaration is bounded twice, on its raw bytes and on its
canonical form (what a report embeds), at most 8192 bytes each, so a report's
`dns.policy` can always be declared back verbatim. An input that fits on the wire
but whose canonical form does not, for example one near the bound that omits
`tempfail`, is refused with 400
`canonical declaration is larger than 8192 bytes`. It also holds at most 256 names
and values in all (each txt owner, each value and each tempfail name counts one);
one more is refused with `declaration has more than 256 names and values`. A
declaration is kept in memory under its inbox label, so the label may be at most
512 bytes: `inbox label is longer than 512 bytes`. Names are ASCII labels of
[A-Za-z0-9_-], folded to lowercase with one trailing dot stripped, at most 253
bytes; a name matches only itself (no wildcard, no IDNA). Values are exact
printable ASCII, never trimmed. Duplicates, an empty values list and a name under
both txt and tempfail are refused, never repaired. Inbox declarations are
process-local and are not persisted; each request freezes one policy snapshot,
and a change wakes no waiter. Real DNS is configured but refused:
`--dns-resolver real` (env SWARMAIL_DNS_RESOLVER) exits with "real DNS is not
supported; declare records with --dns-policy or PUT /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/dns";
`declared` is the default.

swarmail_get_deliverability_report requires string id and admits no other keys.
Under MCP 2025-03-26, missing-version requests included, it returns report
JSON in one text block, isError=false. On 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 the same
report is also structuredContent under a closed outputSchema matching the REST
DeliverabilityReport: severity enum, tagged header/mime_part/link locations, u64
coordinates, at most 256 findings (the 65536-byte bound, order and deduplication
stay producer rules).
Missing mail and failed/unavailable analysis use isError=true without structured
content; malformed arguments use -32602. The March descriptor keeps main's
"with demo and bulk-sender checks" wording as its historical text, with its
(2025-03-26) suffix; modern descriptors state the full current scope and the structured output (decision 0105).

REST assert/await and MCP wait_for_email admit optional no_findings_at_or_above
(info|warning|error). It qualifies ordinary-filter candidates before paging;
failed reports abort, never count as clean. Exact assert counts its snapshot,
including zero, and never subscribes. Example: assert?count=0&no_findings_at_or_above=warning
holds when zero candidates qualify; it is not a universal inbox health assertion.
Wait still requires at least one, even count=0, and keeps ordinary totals/order.
Zero timeout uses completed cache entries only: cold/busy required reports return
unavailable. An incomplete scan at deadline is unavailable; a complete insufficient
scan keeps the usual timeout with its exact count. Shutdown keeps its existing error.
The option is refused on list/count; absent means existing behavior.

For agents (decision 0131): read swarmail_get_deliverability_report for the id of the
message you sent (the id in the 250 2.0.0 OK: stored as {id} reply, or from a wait
or search). Fix each finding from its rule_id, location and fix_hint, then send a NEW
message (stored mail is never edited, decision 0005) and read the new message's
report. Filter by rule_id family (link., html., spam.): under the default DNS policy
the bulk., spf., dkim. and dmarc. findings remain, so no_findings_at_or_above cannot
say that content is clean. An isError, not-found or unavailable report is not a clean
report, and empty findings do not imply deliverability. The report is bounded to 256
findings and 65536 compact bytes and excess is an error, never truncation. rule_set_id
moves when the report's bytes move: ignore unknown members and match rule ids, not whole
bodies. Published fixtures: tests/fixtures/deliverability-agent/ (newsletter-failing.eml,
newsletter-fixed.eml); the eval task newsletter-findings measures this loop.

Cache: 128 Weak-identity slots per Store, exact immutable inputs and rule version,
four admitted blocking jobs retained through cancellation. Up to 256 findings and
65536 compact JSON bytes per cached report. Inclusive metadata limits are
8388608 raw bytes, 65536 per header block (including separator), 262144 aggregate
header bytes, 256 outer entities including root, and depth 32 (root zero).
Complete bounded MIME inspection includes closing boundaries and attached
containers; missing separators, ambiguous/unsupported metadata, encoded multipart,
truncation or exhausted budgets fail without partial success. Embedded messages
stay opaque. No body transfer decoding, SMTP admission change or stored-field
rewrite follows. HTML analysis refuses raw inputs over 8 MiB before MIME parsing,
aggregate decoded HTML over 4 MiB, more than 256 outer MIME parts, depth above 32
(root 0), or lexical nesting above 32. Detected eligible transfer-decode errors,
MIME parse failure and incomplete supported lexical constructs fail the whole
report, without a partial count or success cache entry. Charset replacement
follows pinned mail-parser behavior. These workload limits do not bound prior
parser allocations or total RSS. The lexical inspection proof counts helper reads and length-bounded operations, separately from cursor progress; it excludes MIME-parser internals, allocation, hash collisions and latency. Its fixed linear bound is tested with adversarial inputs and a real rescanning negative control. REST: 404 missing, 503 "deliverability analysis unavailable" (capacity
or deadline) / "deliverability analysis failed" (analysis/size), native JSON error.
Selected pre-removal reads may finish; fresh lookups cannot resurrect removed mail.
Cache loss at restart costs recomputation. These are cache/job bounds, not total
memory or latency promises. #253 owns DNS observation/policy/expiry/wakeup semantics;
#253 shipped no verification: DKIM verification arrives with decision 0125 on
`mail-auth`, offline against the declared keys; SPF and DMARC arrive with decision
0126 on the same crate (below), and ARC is #256; no external spam scorer or service
ships here. The cache key is the selected Weak mail identity (which carries the
row's immutable SMTP envelope observation), the frozen policy snapshot (including
`spf_client_ip`) and the rule set; every authentication fact is a function of
those, so two requests with equal keys get equal facts.

## DKIM verification (`swarmail-html/8`)

Decision 0125 (issue #254): each `DKIM-Signature` field of a stored
message is verified lazily in the report, from the stored bytes, after the SMTP
250. rsa-sha256 and ed25519-sha256, simple and relaxed canonicalization, the body
and header hashes, `l=` and `x=`. A verified signature and an unsigned message
emit nothing; every unverified outcome is an error finding on
`{"kind":"header","name":"dkim-signature","occurrence":k}` (k counts the
message's root DKIM-Signature fields from zero), except a verified signature whose
`l=` covers only a prefix of the body, which is a warning. Keys come only from
the declared DNS map (`PUT /api/v1/inboxes/{inbox}/dns`, record
`<s>._domainkey.<d>`); every name asked inside the DNS policy's grammar is recorded
in `dns.lookups` (a name outside it is refused unasked and not recorded); real DNS
is not supported. A signature is judged at the message's receipt second: `x=` at or
before it (or a literal `x=0` with no `t=`) is expired. The one residual,
`dkim.expired_since_receipt.v1`, is the crate's own wall-clock check, and its
radius is wide: once the host clock passes an `x=` that is after the receipt
second, every verdict for that signature (a pass, the warning and every error
alike) becomes that finding and its key lookups disappear, so a clean report can
later begin to disqualify. `a=`, `v=` and plain decimal `t=`, `x=` and `l=` are
required (`dkim.malformed.v1`). If the verifier's header/body boundary differs from
Swarmail's (a header line without a colon, or a whitespace-only first line), the
message (or a DKIM-Signature field name with a space before the colon) gets one
`dkim.header_boundary_ambiguous.v1` and nothing else, at occurrence 0, or null when
the message has no root DKIM-Signature field. The crate
counts `l=` in raw bytes, RFC 6376 counts canonical ones, so a `body_hash_mismatch`
on a signature with `l=` is not evidence of tampering. At most 16 signature fields
and 128 `h=` names are judged; past either bound one `dkim.limits_exceeded.v1`
finding stands alone.
Rule ids, each at version 1: `dkim.malformed.v1`, `dkim.unsupported.v1`, `dkim.from_unsigned.v1`, `dkim.header_boundary_ambiguous.v1`, `dkim.limits_exceeded.v1`, `dkim.signature_expired.v1`, `dkim.expired_since_receipt.v1`, `dkim.selector_invalid.v1`, `dkim.key_missing.v1`, `dkim.key_invalid.v1`, `dkim.key_revoked.v1`, `dkim.not_evaluated.v1`, `dkim.body_hash_mismatch.v1`, `dkim.signature_mismatch.v1`, `dkim.auid_mismatch.v1`, `dkim.atps_unauthorized.v1`, `dkim.body_length_exceeds.v1`, `dkim.body_length_partial.v1`.
A report also needs its SPF and DMARC evidence and the rest of the checklist to be
clean before it qualifies at a threshold; assert on DKIM rule ids to judge a signer
alone. See the deliverability guide for each rule's hint, passing and failing fixture.

## SPF and DMARC (`swarmail-html/8`)

Decision 0126 (issue #255): SPF for the SMTP envelope and DMARC for the
root From, lazily in the report on the stored bytes after the SMTP 250, on
`mail-auth` with DNS only from the declared policy. A pass emits nothing. The
SMTP session records the TCP peer (IPv4-mapped IPv6 as the IPv4) and the last
HELO/EHLO name in the stored row before the insert, never from a header; REST-seeded
mail and rows from before the columns hold none and are never backfilled. One
`check_host` per message: the MAIL FROM domain, or the HELO name for the null
sender, against the observed address, or against `spf_client_ip` when the policy
declares one (an IP literal, canonical, for every peer; it never makes mail with no
observed peer evaluable). A test over loopback declares `ip4:127.0.0.1` in its
record. Of a name's values only one `v=spf1` counts and two are a permanent error;
one `v=DMARC1` counts (the tag is case-exact, spaces may surround the `=`) and two at
one name are no record there, so the walk goes on. A term that names no mechanism is
an SPF permanent error. The
policy is TXT-only, so `a`, `mx`, `ptr`, `exists` and `%{p}` are not evaluated:
`spf.unsupported_mechanism.v1`, `spf_pass` Unknown, never a failure (a term after
the first match is never reached). Ten DNS-querying terms are admitted and the
eleventh is `spf.permerror.v1`; a target with no record is already a permanent
error, so void lookups need no counter; at most twelve names per SPF evaluation
and eight per DMARC tree walk. DMARC: exactly one root From with one domain (else
`dmarc.from_invalid.v1`; `Email.from` is never read), the RFC 9989 tree walk over
the declared `_dmarc` records, the organizational domain determined offline by
those records alone (`psd=y` marks a public suffix; no list exists), the applied
policy `p=`, `sp=` or `np=` (a name exists when it or a name below it is
declared) stepped down by `t=y`, and `pct=` ignored. Relaxed and strict alignment
(`adkim`, `aspf`) with DKIM signatures that DKIM's own verdicts accept and SPF's
identity domain. Rule ids, each at version 1, severity error unless noted:
`spf.fail.v1`, `spf.softfail.v1`, `spf.neutral.v1`, `spf.none.v1`,
`spf.temperror.v1`, `spf.permerror.v1`, `spf.unsupported_mechanism.v1`,
`spf.not_evaluated.v1` (info), `dmarc.from_invalid.v1`, `dmarc.none.v1`,
`dmarc.temperror.v1`, `dmarc.permerror.v1`, `dmarc.fail.none.v1`,
`dmarc.fail.quarantine.v1`, `dmarc.fail.reject.v1`, `dmarc.not_evaluated.v1`. They
name results as Authentication-Results does (`spf=fail` is `spf.fail.v1`,
`dmarc=fail` is `dmarc.fail.<policy>.v1`). SPF findings sit at header
return-path (occurrence null: the envelope); DMARC findings at the root from.
The one clock: SPF's evaluation starts a monotonic timer in the crate and refuses
a DNS-querying term after 20 seconds, so only a process descheduled for 20 seconds
inside one evaluation turns a verdict into `spf.permerror.v1` (fail-closed; a held
amendment of the no-ambient-time rule, decision 0126 section 8). See the
deliverability guide for each rule's hint, passing and failing fixture.

## Spam signals (`swarmail-spam/1`)

Six built-in, offline, deterministic rules read only the captured message: the
root Subject, the root From display name and the sender's `text/plain` bodies
(decision 0122, accepted). There is no external scorer, network, clock, locale or
configuration; the same stored bytes always give the same findings. Each rule
emits at most one finding per report, severity info or warning (error stays the
bulk checklist's requirement level), so a large message can never flood the
report. They arrived as `swarmail-spam/1`; with the link rules of decision 0121,
the `dns` member of decision 0120, the DKIM rules of decision 0125, the SPF and
DMARC rules of decision 0126 and the weight and total of decision 0122 §2 the
report's `rule_set_id` is now `swarmail-html/8`, so the rule-set version
is recorded in every report and in the cache key. Every finding carries a
`weight` and the report a `total` (see Weight and total below); the weights
named in each rule are the weights the report emits.

Subject means the first root Subject field in wire order, RFC 2047-decoded and
unfolded; From means the first mailbox of the first root From field, display name
decoded. A later duplicate field never substitutes for the first. Letters are
ASCII A–Z/a–z only and case comparison is ASCII-only: no Unicode case folding,
so a non-ASCII letter neither counts as a capital nor as lowercase. Body rules
read eligible text parts: a non-multipart part reached through multipart
containers only, whose type is `text/plain` or absent (RFC 2045 default; a
`multipart/digest` child defaults to `message/rfc822` and is not scanned), that is
not an attachment, does not carry a filename or name parameter and does not sit
under such a part. Embedded `message/*` bodies stay opaque and `text/html` is
never scanned (HTML is #259's surface; HTML-only mail already receives
`bulk.plain_text.v1`). The text is the transfer- and charset-decoded contents. A
body finding is located at the `mime_part` path of the first matching eligible
part in wire order (root `[]`, children by index).

### `spam.subject.all_caps.v1`

- **Matches:** a Subject with at least 8 ASCII letters, none lowercase.
- **Severity:** warning. **Weight:** 3.
- **Location:** `header {name:"subject", occurrence:0}`.
- **Why:** an all-capital subject reads as shouting and is a classic spam signal;
  the 8-letter floor keeps short acronyms such as `RSVP` or `OTP: 123456` clear.
- **Fix hint:** `Write the Subject in sentence case; an all-capital subject reads as shouting and is a common spam signal.`
- **Passing:** `Subject: URGENT` (6 letters) and `Subject: WINTER Sale` (a lowercase letter).
- **Failing:** `Subject: WINTER SALE`.

### `spam.subject.punctuation.v1`

- **Matches:** a Subject containing `!!`, `??` or `$$`.
- **Severity:** info. **Weight:** 1.
- **Location:** `header {name:"subject", occurrence:0}`.
- **Why:** repeated emphasis punctuation is a weak but common sales-spam marker; a
  single `!`, `?` or `$` is ordinary.
- **Fix hint:** `Remove repeated !, ? or $ characters from the Subject.`
- **Passing:** `Subject: Your receipt!`
- **Failing:** `Subject: Your receipt!!`

### `spam.subject.phrases.v1`

- **Matches:** a Subject containing a phrase from the list below.
- **Severity:** warning. **Weight:** 3.
- **Location:** `header {name:"subject", occurrence:0}`.
- **Why:** these are high-pressure sales claims that filters have long weighted.
- **Fix hint:** `Remove high-pressure sales wording from the Subject; see the guide's phrase list.`
- **Passing:** `Subject: Your invoice is ready`
- **Failing:** `Subject: Act now to keep your account`

### `spam.from.display_name_address.v1`

- **Matches:** a From display name containing an address-shaped token
  (`[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+`) that is not, ASCII
  case-insensitively, the mailbox's own address. A group, an empty list or a
  mailbox without an address yields no finding.
- **Severity:** warning. **Weight:** 3.
- **Location:** `header {name:"from", occurrence:0}`.
- **Why:** a different address in the display name is how mail clients are made to
  show a trusted-looking sender; the same address as the real one is harmless.
- **Fix hint:** `Do not put an email address in the From display name unless it is the sending address; a different address there looks like spoofing.`
- **Passing:** `From: "Billing" <billing@example.test>` and `From: "Billing@Example.test" <billing@example.test>`.
- **Failing:** `From: "ceo@bank.example" <billing@example.test>`

### `spam.body.phrases.v1`

- **Matches:** an eligible text part containing a phrase from the list below.
- **Severity:** warning. **Weight:** 3.
- **Location:** `mime_part {path}` of the first matching eligible part.
- **Why:** the same claims as the Subject rule, in the body.
- **Fix hint:** `Remove high-pressure sales wording from the text/plain body; see the guide's phrase list.`
- **Passing:** `Your order has shipped.`
- **Failing:** `Your order has shipped. Act now.`

### `spam.body.zero_width.v1`

- **Matches:** an eligible text part with at least 3 zero-width characters
  (U+200B, U+200C, U+2060, U+FEFF). U+200D (ZWJ) is excluded because emoji
  sequences use it legitimately.
- **Severity:** info. **Weight:** 1.
- **Location:** `mime_part {path}` of the first matching eligible part.
- **Why:** invisible characters inside words are used to hide them from filters; one
  or two are common in pasted text, so the floor is three.
- **Fix hint:** `Remove zero-width characters from the text/plain body; they are used to hide words from filters.`
- **Passing:** a body with two U+200B characters.
- **Failing:** a body with three U+200B characters.

### Phrase list

Fourteen fixed phrases: `act now`, `limited time offer`, `100% free`, `risk-free`,
`risk free`, `you have won`, `you are a winner`, `claim your prize`,
`no credit check`, `double your money`, `make money fast`, `once in a lifetime`,
`this is not spam`, `cash bonus`. A phrase matches ASCII case-insensitively, each
internal space matching one or more of space, tab, CR or LF (so a line-wrapped
phrase matches), with no ASCII letter, digit or `_` immediately before or after it
(`reactnow` and `act nowhere` do not match). Words transactional mail legitimately
uses, such as "urgent", "congratulations" or "verify your account", are
deliberately not listed.

### Spam signal bounds

| input | bound |
|---|---|
| raw message | 8,388,608 bytes, checked before any collector |
| root header block (Subject, From) | 65,536 bytes including the separator |
| MIME parts / depth | 256 including root / 32 (root 0) |
| aggregate decoded eligible text | 4,194,304 bytes, summed over every eligible part before any rule matches |
| spam findings | at most 6, one per rule |

Exceeding the text bound fails the whole report (REST 503 "deliverability
analysis failed", MCP isError), even if an earlier part would have matched: a
truncated scan is refused, never reported as clean. Work is linear: the phrase
matcher is one finite-automaton regex compiled once from the constant list, and
the zero-width count is one pass, so the spam collector inspects at most the
65,536 header bytes plus 4,194,304 text bytes per report, beyond the single
bounded MIME parse. Cost of the bound: a message with more than 4 MiB of decoded
`text/plain`, which earlier rule sets reported on, now fails analysis.

### Signals counted elsewhere

The spam rules do not re-detect what other collectors report. A reader assessing
spam risk should also count `bulk.plain_text.v1` (HTML-only mail),
`bulk.one_click.v1` (no one-click unsubscribe), `bulk.message_id.v1`,
`bulk.date.v1`, `html.image-only.v1` and `html.tracking-pixel.v1`. Every one of
them is already counted: the report's `total` weighs every finding by its
severity (info 1, warning 3, error 10), with `*.not_evaluated.*` findings and
`demo.marker.v1` at zero (Weight and total, below). Link and URL signals are #258's
link rules and DNS policy belongs to #253; the spam rules read no URL and resolve
nothing.

### Weight and total

Decision 0122 §2, accepted on 2026-11-06 and emitted from `swarmail-html/8`,
gives every finding a `weight` and the report a `total`, so no reader has to
invent a weighting and no edge (REST, MCP, the UI) computes a score. Both are
non-negative integers, and each is the **last** key of its object: a finding is
`rule_id`, `location`, `severity`, `fix_hint`, `weight`, and the report is
`rule_set_id`, `findings`, `dns`, `total`. MCP serializes the same report with
sorted keys, where `weight` and `total` also sort last, so no key that was
already served moves.

| severity | weight |
|---|---|
| info | 1 |
| warning | 3 |
| error | 10 |

The weight depends on the severity alone, for every rule family: the demo
marker, the bulk checklist, the HTML heuristics, the link rules, the spam
signals, DKIM, SPF and DMARC. There is no per-id table. Two exceptions weigh 0:
any rule id containing `.not_evaluated.` (a trusted fact that could not be
determined is not evidence about the sender, and a fresh deployment must not
score every message) and `demo.marker.v1` (synthetic).

The `total` is the sum of the findings' weights after the findings are sorted
and exact duplicates are removed, so a duplicate counts once. It is at most
2,560 (256 findings of weight 10). The evaluator computes it inside the byte
bound, so a report served from the cache and a freshly evaluated one are
byte-identical, and a sum that would overflow fails the report and never wraps.

**Predicates ignore weight.** `no_findings_at_or_above` on `assert`, `await`
and `swarmail_wait_for_email` still decides on severity alone, plus the
`temp_fail` rule of decision 0120. A report whose `total` is 0 is not "clean"
(a sole `bulk.*.not_evaluated.v1` error weighs 0 and still refuses at `error`),
and a large `total` is not "dirty" (256 info findings total 256 and still
qualify at `warning`).

**Cost.** The two keys are part of the report's 65,536-byte bound: about 11 to
12 bytes per finding and up to 14 for the total. A message whose report was just
under the bound before `swarmail-html/8` can now fail analysis, which is the
bound doing its job (it counts what is served).

### Known false negatives and positives

False negatives: HTML-only spam wording, phrases outside the fixed list, phrases
split by tags or inserted characters, non-ASCII look-alike letters, a partly
shouted subject with any lowercase letter, and spam with a clean Subject and body
but a bad link or sender (not read here). False positives: a legitimate subject in
capitals of 8 or more letters, a genuine "limited time offer" in a newsletter, and
a newsletter whose display name repeats a different mailbox, or a bare address followed by a comment holding another address (the parser reads the comment as the display name). An empty report does
not mean the message will reach the inbox.

### Rule-set version history

`swarmail-demo/1` (synthetic demo marker), `swarmail-bulk/1` (bulk-sender
checklist), `swarmail-html/2` and `swarmail-html/3` (HTML heuristics), then
`swarmail-spam/1` (these six rules; no existing rule changed meaning), then
`swarmail-html/4` (the five link rules of proposed 0121, integrated after
`swarmail-spam/1`; no existing rule changed meaning), then
`swarmail-html/5` (the required `dns` report member of proposed 0120,
integrated after `swarmail-html/4`; no rule changed meaning), then
`swarmail-html/6` (the eighteen DKIM rules of proposed 0125, integrated after
`swarmail-html/5`; no existing rule changed meaning), then
`swarmail-html/7` (the sixteen SPF and DMARC rules of proposed 0126, integrated
after `swarmail-html/6`; the three authentication entries of the bulk checklist
now read evaluated facts, so their findings changed), then
`swarmail-html/8` (the per-finding `weight` and the report `total` of decision
0122 §2, integrated after `swarmail-html/7`; no rule changed meaning, and every
report gained the two keys). A change to
any rule's meaning, hint, location or order requires a new id.
